title: Scaling and Renormalization in Neural Networks: An Effective Renormalization-Group Description of Grokking
authors: Min Chen, Junqi Wang, Zeguan Wu, Wenhao Huang, Junyu Liu
abstract: Grokking is a delayed transition from memorization to generalization in deep neural networks (NNs). We examine whether scaling and renormalization group (RG) theories can describe this dynamics, establishing a quantitative physical framework for neural generalization transitions. For modular addition on a two-layer NN, an ensemble of trained models defines an order parameter (the squared weight norm) and fluctuation proxies for the heat capacity and the susceptibility, with training epoch and weight decay serving as thermal and field control coordinates. To bridge neural architectures to real-space RG, we construct an exact coupling matrix via a second-order expansion of the loss with respect to per-neuron norms and use its Fiedler vector to define an effective geometry. This spectral ordering yields a monotonic spatial decay of coupling strength that is absent under random permutations. We then execute real-space RG by block-spin aggregating adjacent neurons and parameterizing the coupling matrix into off-diagonal band strengths. Linearizing this local RG map yields relevant scaling exponents and five derived critical exponents, with direct empirical estimates matching RG predictions within 1-10%. Overall, our framework provides a consistent effective description of grokking, suggesting the scaling and renormalization group formalism as a tool to investigate NN dynamics.
summary: This paper applies Renormalization Group (RG) theory, traditionally used for phase transitions, to model 'grokking'—the delayed generalization in neural networks. By mapping training dynamics onto a statistical physics Hamiltonian, the authors derive critical exponents that successfully describe the transition, establishing a quantitative physical framework for NN generalization.
main_problem: To determine if scaling and Renormalization Group (RG) theories can provide a quantitative physical framework to describe "grokking"—the delayed transition from memorization to generalization in deep neural networks (NNs).
main_result: The framework provides a consistent effective description of grokking, showing that critical exponents derived from the RG approach match empirical estimates from NN training dynamics within 1-10%.
method: The authors construct an effective Hamiltonian and apply real-space RG techniques, mapping NN training dynamics onto established critical phenomena scaling laws.
model_or_system: The system is a deep neural network (specifically, a two-layer perceptron trained on modular addition), whose dynamics are mapped onto a lattice spin model where training epochs act as inverse temperature and weight decay acts as a field.
key_observables:
Order parameter (squared weight norm), Susceptibility ($\chi_S$), Heat Capacity ($C_H$), and critical exponents ($\alpha,  eta, \gamma, 
u, \delta$).
important_parameters: Training epoch ($e$), weight decay ($\lambda$), and the effective spatial dimension ($d=1$) derived from the Fiedler vector ordering.
main_assumptions: The primary assumptions involve mapping thermodynamic quantities (like variance of loss) to physical observables and assuming that the coupling structure can be effectively ordered into a 1D chain using spectral methods.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the complementary routes to critical exponent determination (RG vs. Dictionary), show the spectral ordering of couplings, and display the parameter cloud mapping between RG coordinates and observed training parameters.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes a 'physical dictionary' mapping NN observables to thermodynamic quantities. It then develops the RG framework by constructing a coupling matrix via loss expansion and ordering it using the Fiedler vector. Finally, it executes real-space RG and derives scaling exponents, comparing them to direct estimates.
why_interesting: The application of rigorous critical phenomena tools (RG, scaling laws) to the non-equilibrium dynamics of machine learning models provides a powerful, physics-based lens for understanding generalization.
analysis_basis: full PDF text, analyzed in chunks

figures.caption: Figure 1: Overview. From trained NNs (left), the critical exponents of grokking are obtained via two complementary routes. RG route (top): each hidden neuron carries a spin si, its squared weight norm, while each neuron pair is connected by a coupling Jij derived from the loss Hessian. Ordering the neurons on a chain using the Fiedler vector of this coupling graph enables adjacent neurons to be merged into blocks, where a linear fit of the coarsened couplings yields yt and yh, from which five critical exponents follow (Sections 3.2–3.3).
